en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Fourth Chapter
The Discourse on Entering the Path of Certainty:
Did the Bodhisatta enter the path of certainty and practice the holy life during the dispensation of the Blessed One Kassapa?
Yes, he did.
Was the Bodhisatta a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Was the Bodhisatta a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa?
“Yes,” you say.
“Having been a disciple, one becomes a Buddha”?
You must not say so … [and so on] …
Is it the case that one becomes a Buddha after having been a disciple?
Yes. Is such a person one who has followed a tradition? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it a tradition? Yes.
Is it not the case that the Blessed One is self-enlightened?
Yes, it is.
If the Blessed One is indeed self-enlightened, then certainly, it should not be said: [that he was taught by another].
“[They are] ‘those who have been instructed. [Question:
Was the Bodhisatta one who had entered the fixed course of rightness and was practicing the holy life under the dispensation of the Blessed One Kassapa?
[Answer: Yes.
"Did the Blessed One awaken to only three fruits of asceticism at the foot of the Bodhi tree?
"One should not say so... [etc.
"...Is it not the case that the Blessed One awakened to all four fruits of asceticism at the foot of the Bodhi tree?"
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If the four fruits of asceticism were fully awakened to by the Blessed One at the foot of the Bodhi tree, then surely it should not be said:
‘The Bodhisatta had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the dispensation of the Blessed Kassapa.’”
The Bodhisatta had entered the fixed course of rightness and was living the holy life under the Blessed One Kassapa—
yes? He performed ascetic practices— yes?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Could a person endowed with vision perform difficult deeds?
“One should not say so” … [and so on] …
Did the Bodhisatta practice self-mortification and acknowledge another teacher?
Yes. Would a person endowed with right vision acknowledge another teacher? No.

It should not be said so … [as before] … Did the Venerable Ānanda enter the fixed course of rightness in the Blessed One’s teaching and lead the holy life? Did the Venerable Ānanda become a disciple of the Blessed One?
Yes, he did.
Was the Bodhisatta one who had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One Kassapa, such that he was a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa?
You should not say so... [and so on] ...

Was the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī one who had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One, such that the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī were disciples of the Blessed One?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Was the Bodhisatta one who had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One Kassapa; was the Bodhisatta a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa?
You must not say so… [and so on]… No, you must not.
The Bodhisatta had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One Kassapa, yet he was not a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa?
Yes.
Then, the Venerable Ānanda had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One, yet he was not a disciple of the Blessed One?
It should not be said so...
[as before] ...Was the Bodhisatta one who had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One Kassapa, yet was not a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa?
Yes, he was.
“Were the householder Citta and Hatthaka Āḷavaka, who had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One’s teaching, not disciples of the Blessed One?
One should certainly not say so… [and so on] …Was the Bodhisatta,
who had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One Kassapa’s teaching, not a disciple of the Blessed One Kassapa?”
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does a disciple who has transcended birth cease to be a disciple?
One should not say so… [and so on]… No.
Is it not to be said that the Bodhisatta, during the dispensation of the Blessed One Kassapa, had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life?
Yes, it should be so affirmed.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Ānanda, under the Blessed One Kassapa I lived the holy life for the sake of future full enlightenment”?
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes, [you say] so.
In that case, it should not be said:
“The Bodhisatta, in the dispensation of the Blessed One Kassapa, had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life.”
Is it not the case that the Bodhisatta had entered the fixed course of certainty and was practicing the holy life under the dispensation of the Blessed One Kassapa?
Yes, it is.
Has this not been said by the Blessed One:
“I am the conqueror of all, the knower of all;
I am unsullied by any phenomena.
Having relinquished everything, I am liberated through the destruction of craving.”
Having realized it for myself, whom should I point to? I have no teacher,
and my equal is not found.
In this world with its gods,
there is no one who is my equal;
for I am indeed the Worthy One (Arahant) in the world.
I am the unsurpassed Teacher;
I alone am the perfectly awakened Buddha,
cooled and extinguished.
I shall go to the city of Kāsi to set in motion the Wheel of Dhamma,
for this world has become blind.
“I shall beat the drum of the Deathless.
“Friend, according to what you claim, you are an Arahant, a Conqueror of the Infinite.
“The Conquerors are indeed like me.”
Those who have attained the destruction of the taints,
by whom evil states have been conquered—
therefore, Upaka, I am a Conqueror.”
Is it indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“The Bodhisatta had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One Kassapa.
Is it true that the Bodhisatta had entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the Blessed One Kassapa?
Yes, it is true.
"Was it not said by the Blessed One:
'Bhikkhus, regarding these things unheard of before, the eye arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, light arose:
"This is the noble truth of suffering. Bhikkhus, regarding this noble truth of suffering, "it must be fully understood"—thus, bhikkhus...'"?
“‘The full understanding has been achieved,’ bhikkhus— regarding these things unheard of before, vision arose in me … light arose in me.
‘This is the noble truth of the origin of suffering,’ bhikkhus … ‘But this noble truth of the origin of suffering must be abandoned,’ bhikkhus …”
"It has been abandoned by me," monks...
"This is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering," monks...
"Furthermore, this noble truth of the cessation of suffering is to be realized," monks... [and so on].
“‘This has been realized by me,

monks’ … ‘This is the noble truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This noble truth of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering must be developed by me,’ monks. …pe…
“‘It has been developed,’ monks, regarding these states unheard of by me before, vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true insight arose, and light arose.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, it should not be said:
"The Bodhisatta entered the fixed course of rightness and lived the holy life under the dispensation of the Blessed One Kassapa.
The Discussion on Entering the Fixed Course is finished.
